author: Secretariat
title: Semana Internacional Contra el Impago de Salarios
content:
Del 12 al 18 de octubre se celebra la Semana de la Asociación Internacional de los Trabajadores (AIT) contra el impago de salarios. La lucha contra el impago de salarios es una campaña permanente de la AIT, y esta semana es el momento en que animamos a los sindicatos y otras organizaciones a alzar la voz sobre este tema.

Señalamos que el impago de salarios puede adoptar diversas formas:

- falta total de pago por el trabajo realizado - pago insuficiente de diversa índole, incluyendo obligar a las personas a realizar horas extra sin remuneración adicional, pagar menos de la tarifa acordada, pagar menos de la tarifa legal o de lo estipulado en un convenio colectivo, etc. - obligar a las personas a trabajar bajo contratos inadecuados para privarlas de prestaciones legales, como vacaciones pagadas o baja por enfermedad - deducciones injustificadas del salario - periodos de prueba, de formación o prácticas no remunerados e ilegales

… por citar solo algunas de las formas en que los patrones roban a los trabajadores el dinero que han ganado.

Puedes participar en esta semana de diferentes maneras: desde republicar nuestros artículos o escribir uno propio, hasta emprender acciones directas contra una empresa donde se hayan producido estos problemas o contactar a los trabajadores de dicho lugar para animarles a actuar.

author: Secretariat
title: IWA Week Against Unpaid Wages
content:
October 12-18 is the International Workers' Association Week Against Unpaid Wages. The fight against unpaid wages is a permanent campaign of the IWA and the week is when we encourage the unions and other organizations to make some noise about this topic.

We point out that unpaid wages can take various forms:

- complete lack of payment for work performed - underpayment of different kinds including forcing people to work overtime without extra payment, paying less than the agreed rate, paying less than the legal rate or less than required by a collective agreement, etc. - forcing people to work on the wrong kind of contract so they are ineligible for statutory benefits, such as paid vacation or sick leave - unjustified deductions from the salary - illegal unpaid probationary periods, training periods and internships

… just to name a few of the ways that bosses rob the workers of the money they have earned.

You can participate in this Week in different ways – ranging from republishing our articles, to writing one of your own, from taking direct against a business where problems have occured to contacting workers in such a place and encouraging them to take action.

And, if you haven't read this yet, we recommend an article written by comrades from South Korea which talks about some of the issues with unpaid wages in that country. https://iwa-ait.org/content/iwa-campaign-agains

author: Secretariat
title: IWA Campaign Against Wage Theft in Korea
content:
Every year in October, the International Workers' Association (IWA-AIT), a global federation of anarcho-syndicalist organizations, launches its annual campaign against wage theft.

This year's campaign will take place from October 12th to October 16th.

Officially launched in 2020 and celebrating its 6th anniversary this year, this campaign aims to expose all forms of wage theft that plague workers worldwide and encourages direct action to reclaim stolen rights.

Wage theft, in this context, is not simply about employers delaying salaries by a few days.

Any scheme or illegal practice used by employers under a capitalist system to reduce labor costs and maximize profits constitutes wage theft, not just wage delay.

These acts of wage theft occur across borders and, in particular, in South Korea, subtle forms of capital exploitation and structural wage theft continue to this day.

First, there is the deprivation of rights disguised as legal compliance. This refers to the practice of forcing workers, even those under the supervision and control of employers, to become "sham freelancers" or enter into service/civil contracts to save on labor costs and avoid obligations related to four major social insurance programs and severance pay.
